clinician.final_diagnosis: ocular Toxoplasmosis involving his right eye
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old male presented with decreased vision in his right eye for five days, exhibiting choroidoretinopathy on fundus examination and SD-OCT findings consistent with active and old lesions. Initial suspicion of parasitic infection led to collection of aqueous humor and serum samples. Laboratory analysis confirmed the presence of Toxoplasma DNA, positive Toxoplasma IgG and IgM in aqueous humor, and positive serum Toxoplasma IgG. The Goldmann-Witmer coefficient for T. gondii was significantly elevated. Other infectious causes such as HIV, Herpes, Varicella, CMV, and syphilis were ruled out by negative antibody tests.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with decreased vision in the right eye and characteristic fundus lesions (round lesion with clear boundary and pigmentation, yellow-white retinochoroidal lesion with poorly defined borders) and SD-OCT findings (mild edema, serous detachment in active lesions, atrophy/thinning in old lesions).
Toxoplasma DNA was detectable in the aqueous humor sample.
Toxoplasma immunoglobulin G (IgG) and immunoglobulin M (IgM) were positive in the aqueous humor.
Serum Toxoplasma IgG was positive (10.04 IU/mL; reference range: 0–7.2 IU/mL).
The Goldmann-Witmer coefficient value of T. gondii was 12 (reference range 0–2), indicating intraocular antibody production.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative for anti-Herpes and anti-Varicella antibodies

remaining_uncertainties: Specific treatment regimen administered for ocular Toxoplasmosis
